title: CGM sensor — interstitial delay, noise, drift, discontinuities (Rebrin & Steil 1999)

caption.scope: CGM sensor model showing the four sources of deviation between true plasma glucose G and the value cgmBG displayed to the player, following the two-compartment interstitial delay framework of Rebrin & Steil (Rebrin K, Steil GM et al., Am J Physiol 277:E561-E571, 1999). (1) Interstitial compartment C follows G with first-order kinetics at ka_int = 0.073 /min (τ ≈ 14 min), producing a low-pass lag that causes CGM to under-read during rapidly rising BG and over-read during rapid falls. (2) Gaussian sensor noise with σ ≈ 0.03 · BG mmol/L, calibrated from ~34 000 real Libre 2 readings. (3) Slow sinusoidal drift (period 4–8 h, amplitude 0.3–0.7 mmol/L) representing systematic sensor bias. (4) Rare discontinuities (~0.7 per simulated day, magnitude up to ±2 mmol/L) for compression and calibration artefacts. The signal generators noise, drift, and jump are not ODE states — they are additive corrections computed each simulation tick and summed onto C to produce cgmBG.

variables.definition: true plasma glucose concentration derived from Hovorka model: G = Q1 / V_G (mmol/L)
interstitial fluid glucose — the physiological quantity sensed by the CGM electrode (mmol/L)
displayed CGM reading after all signal corrections are applied (mmol/L)
sensor noise generator: Gaussian draw scaled by BG, σ ≈ 0.03 · BG; calibrated to Libre 2 in-vivo data
drift generator: sinusoidal bias, period U(4, 8) h, amplitude U(0.3, 0.7) mmol/L
discontinuity generator: Poisson-rate events (~0.7 per simulated day), magnitude up to ±2 mmol/L, modelling compression and calibration artefacts
plasma-to-interstitium glucose diffusion rate constant = 0.073 /min (τ ≈ 14 min); from Rebrin & Steil 1999
instantaneous noise sample added each tick: ε ~ N(0, σ²), σ = 0.03 · BG (Box-Muller)
instantaneous drift value sampled from the running sine generator and added to C
instantaneous discontinuity offset added to C on each stochastic event
